top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are a mature, experimentally demonstrated advance: magic-wavelength trapping lets many atoms be interrogated at once with motional and light-shift errors cancelled, reaching about 1e-18 fractional uncertainty and opening a new regime in the measurement of time. The two-laureate allocation matches the invention and realization, the citation scope is clean, and all eight members support it, so no award is clearly inferior.
